newsitem.title: CHINA: China budget deficit at 60.9 billion yuan in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China budget deficit at 60.9 billion yuan in 1996.

text.p: China's budget deficit was 60.884 billion yuan ($7.3 billion) in 1996, with revenues and expenditures growing faster than official expectations, the Xinhua news agency on Wednesday quoted Minister of Finance Liu Zhongli as saying.
Total central government revenues were 426.495 billion yuan in 1996 while expenditures were 487.379 billion yuan, Liu said in a report to the National People's Congress, or parliament.
The deficit was mainly due to spending to help support less developed central and western regions, to stem losses in grain enterprises, and on disaster relief, Liu said.
Liu said implementation of the 1996 budget had been hampered by an over-reliance on debt, tax evasion and too-loose controls over expenditures but did not elaborate.
Revenues last year were 8.368 billion yuan higher than the budget forecast and rose 10.3 percent from the previous year, he said.
Spending was 7.81 billion yuan higher than budget forecasts and was up 7.6 percent from the year before, he said.
Revenue directly collected by the central government hit 366.107 billion yuan while that handed over to Beijing by local governments was 60.388 billion yuan, he said.
Chinese officials have said they expected the budget deficit to be about 60 billion yuan in 1996 and say they are aiming for 56 billion yuan this year.
